headline: High risk of shared-repo write conflicts and cascading bad edits; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider and Plandex have no documented shared clipboard/MCP channel, so direct injection is not the default path. However, both can read and write repo files, and Aider explicitly treats git-tracked files as inputs while Plandex stages project changes, so malicious content in shared files could influence the other agent if operators bridge them through the repo.
conditions: IF operators use the shared repository as a handoff channel between Aider and Plandex, injected instructions in files can be re-read by the other agent.
IF either agent is asked to summarize or act on untrusted repo text, prompt-like content may be followed as instructions.
mitigations: Keep handoff files separate from task files.
Prefix untrusted text with explicit non-instruction markers.
Require human review before one agent consumes the other's output.
Use a dedicated scratch branch for inter-agent exchange.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-originated content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read the filesystem and have broad network egress, so sensitive repo contents can flow into model-provider APIs in default coding workflows. Aider explicitly handles model provider API keys and git-tracked files; Plandex also sends project context to a model provider or Plandex Cloud/self-hosted server. Shared workspace plus outbound inference creates a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at a repository containing secrets or regulated data, that content may be transmitted to external model services.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace, data touched by one can be exposed to the other's outbound requests.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared repo before use.
Use local-only or self-hosted model endpoints.
Restrict both agents to a sanitized subdirectory.
Rotate any credentials present in the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before outbound calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write files, and modify git state, and Aider shares state via a shared git repo while Plandex shares state via a server backend. In a shared repository, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide without locking, making destructive overwrite or merge-conflict loss plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are allowed to write the same git working tree, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF either agent auto-applies changes while the other is mid-plan, git state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Disable auto-apply for one agent during overlap.
Serialize write access with a simple operator checklist.
Commit after each agent finishes a turn.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or orchestrator arbitration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code edits directly and Plandex can stage and apply multi-step plans, so one agent's output can become the other's input and then be acted on without strong verification. That creates a clear cascade path where an incorrect patch or plan is amplified into further edits or commits, especially when both are operating on the same repo.
conditions: IF Plandex consumes Aider-generated diffs or summaries as authoritative, errors can propagate into staged changes.
IF Aider is asked to implement Plandex-produced plans without independent review, incorrect assumptions can be committed.
mitigations: Require a human diff review between agents.
Ask each agent to restate assumptions before acting.
Limit each turn to one small change set.
Run tests after every handoff.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates before apply.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding tools with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling of source code and git history. Aider additionally handles model-provider API keys and broad egress, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data mismatch against Plandex.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into the shared repo, compliance review is required before use.
IF either agent is connected to a provider with stricter retention than the other, policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the repo.
Use a documented data-handling policy.
Prefer self-hosted inference for sensitive projects.
Review provider retention settings.
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls.
